newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sends "letter of serious doubts" to Stena/P&O.
newsitem.headline: EU sends "letter of serious doubts" to Stena/P&O.

text.p: The European Commission on Tuesday sent a letter to Britain's P&O and Sweden's Stena Line setting out its competition concerns about the ferry operators' planned joint venture in the English Channel.
The European Union executive had a number of concerns which were included in its so-called "letter of serious doubts," EU sources said.

"I think everything is possible at this point. It is possible that it (the deal) will get an exemption and it is possible that it might be prohibited," one source said. "But there is plenty of scope I think for negotiation."
One of the Commission's concerns was the combined strength of the Stena/P&O venture and Le Shuttle, the car-train service through the Channel Tunnel, on the cross-Channel market.

"It would be fairly clear that that would be a concern of any competition authority if you got a market where there are five players and two of them have between them 80 percent of the market or more," the source said.

P&O, the Peninsular and Orient Navigation Company, and Stena plan to merge operations across the Channel, notably on the lucrative Dover-Calais route where they will run services approximately every 45 minutes. The deal is also under investigation by British competition authorities.

The Commission's letter does not include any proposals on what the firms could to meet the concerns about the deal's impact on competition. EU sources said it was up to the companies to come back with comments and proposals.

P&O said last week it was confident its proposed joint venture with Stena would go ahead, and Stena's vice president for finance, Anders Hedberg, said it would be a major surprise if the Commission rejected the deal. But he expected that the Commission would ask for changes.
There is no deadline for the Commission to make a final ruling.
